clone.description: Fetch a Git repository from GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps or your own server, so the steps after this one can commit to it, push it and pull it. The repository is kept for this run; pass this step's result to those steps. A private repository needs a token (https) or an SSH key (ssh), stored as a workspace secret.
clone.name: clone

parameters.description: The repository's address, as its host shows it under Clone: https://github.com/acme/website.git, or for ssh git@github.com:acme/website.git.
parameters.name: url

parameters.description: The branch to start on. Leave empty for the repository's default branch.
parameters.name: branch

parameters.description: How many commits of history to fetch. Leave empty for all of it; 1 is fastest when the workflow only needs the latest files, and still lets it commit and push.
parameters.name: depth

parameters.description: For an https address with a token: the name to send with it. GitHub, GitLab and Azure DevOps take any name, so it can be left empty; Bitbucket needs your username with an app password, or x-token-auth with an access token.
parameters.name: username

parameters.description: For an https address: the token or password that may read it, such as a GitHub personal access token. Store it as a workspace secret and put @secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN here, so it is never kept in the workflow. A public repository needs none to clone or pull.
parameters.name: password

parameters.description: For an ssh address (git@github.com:acme/website.git): the private key whose public half is added to the repository or the account. Store the whole key, from BEGIN to END, as a workspace secret and reference it here.
parameters.name: ssh_private_key

returns.description: The cloned repository: 'repository' is what the Commit, Push and Pull steps take, with the branch it is on, its latest commit and message, and its files.

branch.description: The branch it is on, or null when it was cloned at a tag.

commit.description: The latest commit's id, or null for an empty repository.

file_count.description: How many files the repository has on this branch.

files.description: The paths of the repository's files on this branch, up to the first thousand.

repository.description: The repository, for the Commit, Push and Pull steps' Repository field.

url.description: The address it was cloned from.

commit.description: Write files into a cloned repository and record the changes as a commit with a message. A file's content can be text, data from earlier steps (saved as JSON), or a file an earlier step made or downloaded. Nothing reaches the host until a Push changes step.
commit.name: commit

parameters.description: The repository from a Clone a repository step earlier in this workflow: pick that step's result, such as @cloned.
parameters.name: repository

parameters.description: What the commit changes, such as 'Update the autumn price list'.
parameters.name: message

parameters.description: Each file's path in the repository and what to put in it: text as it is, a list or record as JSON, or a file from an earlier step (its doc_ id). A file that isn't there yet is created, folders and all.
parameters.name: files

parameters.description: Paths of files or folders to remove from the repository.
parameters.name: delete

parameters.description: Leave empty to commit every change in the repository. Otherwise, only changes under these paths are committed.
parameters.name: paths

parameters.description: The branch to commit on. Leave empty for the branch the repository is on; a branch that doesn't exist yet is created, which is how a workflow prepares a pull request.
parameters.name: branch

parameters.description: Who the commit is by. Lodol when left empty.
parameters.name: author_name

parameters.description: The author's email address, which hosts use to link the commit to an account.
parameters.name: author_email

returns.description: The commit made: its id and the files it changed. When the files were already as written, 'committed' is false and there is no commit.

branch.description: The branch the commit is on.

committed.description: Whether there was anything to commit.

repository.description: The repository, for the steps after this one.

short_commit.description: The first seven characters of the id.

pull.description: Bring the latest commits from the repository's host into the cloned repository, so the workflow works from, and commits on top of, what is there now.
pull.name: pull

parameters.description: The repository from a Clone a repository step earlier in this workflow: pick that step's result, such as @cloned.
parameters.name: repository

parameters.description: The branch to pull. Leave empty for the branch the repository is on.
parameters.name: branch

parameters.description: For an https address with a token: the name to send with it. GitHub, GitLab and Azure DevOps take any name, so it can be left empty; Bitbucket needs your username with an app password, or x-token-auth with an access token.
parameters.name: username

parameters.description: For an https address: the token or password that may read it, such as a GitHub personal access token. Store it as a workspace secret and put @secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN here, so it is never kept in the workflow. A public repository needs none to clone or pull.
parameters.name: password

parameters.description: For an ssh address (git@github.com:acme/website.git): the private key whose public half is added to the repository or the account. Store the whole key, from BEGIN to END, as a workspace secret and reference it here.
parameters.name: ssh_private_key

returns.description: The branch after the pull: its latest commit, whether anything came in ('updated'), which files changed, and the repository's files now.

commit.description: The latest commit's id after the pull.

file_count.description: How many files the repository has on this branch.

files.description: The paths of the repository's files on this branch, up to the first thousand.

previous_commit.description: The latest commit's id before it.

repository.description: The repository, for the steps after this one.

push.description: Send the commits made in this workflow to the repository's host, so they show up on GitHub, GitLab or wherever it lives. Pushing needs a token or key with write access.
push.name: push

parameters.description: The repository from a Clone a repository step earlier in this workflow: pick that step's result, such as @cloned.
parameters.name: repository

parameters.description: The branch to push. Leave empty for the branch the repository is on.
parameters.name: branch

parameters.description: Leave empty to push back to where the repository was cloned from, or give another repository's address to push there instead.
parameters.name: remote

parameters.description: Replace the branch on the host even when it has commits this copy doesn't. Off, a push behind the host is refused, which is the safe default.
parameters.name: force

parameters.description: For an https address with a token: the name to send with it. GitHub, GitLab and Azure DevOps take any name, so it can be left empty; Bitbucket needs your username with an app password, or x-token-auth with an access token.
parameters.name: username

parameters.description: For an https address: the token or password that may push to it, such as a GitHub personal access token. Store it as a workspace secret and put @secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN here, so it is never kept in the workflow. A public repository needs none to clone or pull.
parameters.name: password

parameters.description: For an ssh address (git@github.com:acme/website.git): the private key whose public half is added to the repository or the account. Store the whole key, from BEGIN to END, as a workspace secret and reference it here.
parameters.name: ssh_private_key

returns.description: What was pushed: the branch, the commit it is now at on the host, and whether anything moved ('pushed'), or the host already had it all ('up_to_date').

commit.description: The commit the branch is now at.

pushed.description: Whether the host received new commits.

repository.description: The repository, for the steps after this one.

summary.description: Git's own summary of the push, such as 9fceb02..a1b2c3d or [new branch].

up_to_date.description: Whether the host already had them all.

description: Clone a repository, commit changes to it, and push to or pull from GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket or any Git server.
